In the Shrimad Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddhakanda

730

Bears, lions, boars, buffaloes, elephants, and deer were startled by that sound and fled in terror in all ten directions. There stood the Trikuta mountain peak, towering and touching the sky. It was covered on all sides with flowers and shone like pure gold. It was a hundred yojanas wide, immaculate, beautiful to behold, smooth, magnificent, and large, inaccessible even to birds. It was difficult to ascend even in thought, let alone by people in action. Established upon that peak was Lanka, protected by Ravana. It was a hundred yojanas wide and thirty yojanas long. That city, with its high gatehouses resembling white clouds, was adorned with walls of gold and silver. Lanka was decorated with palaces and heavenly chariots. Like the sky between the clouds at the end of the summer heat, the palace in that city was embellished with a thousand pillars. Resembling the peak of Mount Kailasa and appearing to scrape the sky, that structure was the jewel of the demon king's city. It was guarded constantly by a full hundred demons. Rama, the elder brother of Lakshmana, who was endowed with majesty, beheld that prosperous and wealthy city of Ravana, which was pleasing, full of forests, graced by mountains, decorated with gardens varied with diverse minerals, echoing with the sounds of many birds, frequented by many animals, covered with various flowers, and inhabited by many demons, along with the monkeys. Seeing that city, which was crowded with great houses, the elder brother of Lakshmana, who was powerful, became astonished at the city that rivaled the celestial ones.

Rama, with his great army, saw that city which was filled with jewels, had many arrangements, was decorated with rows of palaces, and had prominent gates with great mechanical devices.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth sarga, titled "The Sight of Lanka," in the Yuddhakanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the primordial epic consisting of twenty-four thousand verses.

---

### Fortieth Sarga
**The Duel between Ravana and Sugriva**

Then Rama, accompanied by Sugriva and surrounded by monkey leaders, ascended the summit of Mount Suvela, which measured two yojanas in circumference. Having stayed there for a moment, while looking in all ten directions, he saw Lanka, which was well-laid out and adorned with beautiful forests, built on the lovely peak of Trikuta by Vishvakarma. He saw the lord of the demons, who was difficult to approach, stationed on the pinnacle of a gatehouse. He was bordered by white chowries <note>whisks made of yak tails, used as a sign of royalty</note> and adorned with a victory parasol. He was smeared with red sandalwood and decorated with jewel ornaments. He resembled a dark cloud and was dressed in garments covered with gold. His chest bore scars from the tips of the tusks of Airavata <note>the elephant of the god Indra</note>. He was wrapped in a red garment with the hue of a rabbit's blood <note>a shade of deep crimson</note>, appearing like a cloud mass in the sky wrapped in the light of the evening sun. As the lord of the monkeys and also Raghava <note>Rama</note> were watching, Sugriva suddenly rose up at the sight of the lord of the demons.

<note>1. This half-verse is not present in manuscript 'Ka'.</note>

<summary>This text describes the terrifying impact of the monkey army's arrival on the creatures surrounding Lanka, followed by a detailed depiction of the city's golden architecture and formidable fortifications. It concludes with Rama and the monkey leaders ascending Mount Suvela to scout the city, leading to a direct visual confrontation between Sugriva and Ravana.</summary>
